r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command ships with a <fowler-pass-record-path> placeholder; record() runs that command and refuses `pass` while it fails. NORMAL PATH -- resolve the placeholder to the real record path when you INSTANTIATE this survey from the template, before you claim: it is an instantiation-time substitution exactly like <work-id> on line 2. That is the documented route and the one you should be on. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record later moves or the path you substituted was wrong, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

c5-scopedlimit.title: Scoped limit written in docs and not overclaimed
c5-scopedlimit.imperative: Check docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md states the limit plainly and nothing elsewhere contradicts it.
c5-scopedlimit.finding: BLOCKING. The scoped limit IS written into docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md ('The limit -- what this cannot observe', plus 'records begins, not work' and 'never this run was compliant'), and none of that is contradicted elsewhere. But a SECOND limit -- the one that decides whether the observable survives to the seam -- is both unstated and actively contradicted, in the doc AND in the one rendered compliance line. Measured, not argued (probe_clearing.py, real CLI, real gauge): at/over hard, 'advance --mechanical' is REFUSED by g2's no-silent-close rule, so the ONLY legal close is 'advance --why', which appends a new why-record, which supersedes EVERY existing ledger entry, which empties the selector and removes the rendered line. So the mandated close is guaranteed to clear the rendered signal. The shipped line ends 'Closing this gate does not clear the record.' -- I closed that exact gate and the line vanished. Doc says the understanding moves on when 'a fresh agent records its own why', but the mechanism cannot tell a fresh agent from the offender, and the offender's own close is the likeliest superseder. Net: across a 3-gate runaway with 3 recorded over-the-line begins, the rendered signal never claimed more than 2 and was ABSENT at the seam -- green in both worlds, the exact failure mode this gate exists to prevent.

a1-whyref.title: ATTACK: ninth field why_ref reverses critic finding 14
a1-whyref.imperative: Is it genuinely irrecoverable? Is N7's 12-test blast radius load-bearingness or wide coupling?
a1-whyref.finding: ATTACKED in both directions; I independently CONFIRM keeping the field, and I do NOT accept N7 as the reason. (a) Irrecoverable? Yes, in the sense the predicate needs. _latest_why_record's answer is time-dependent in a way the trail cannot replay: a record is live only if no LATER reopen-marker names its gate, so reopens appended AFTER the trip change what a naive 'as of now' derivation returns, and reconstructing 'as of then' requires truncating the trail by timestamp. I measured the timestamps -- _now() is microsecond-precision (not second, as the implementer assumed), so pure ordering is usually unambiguous, but ordering is not the problem; replaying the supersede rule is. Also a recorded fact is auditable where a derived one drifts if _latest_why_record's semantics change. Critic finding 14's 'recoverable from why_trail' is wrong on the supersede rule, not just on granularity. (b) N7's 12 tests are NOT evidence for the field. N7 sets why_ref to None, which makes every entry fail the keying, which is behaviourally the same as dead-coding the selector (N11, 11 tests, largely the same set). N7 proves the KEYING is load-bearing; it cannot distinguish 'record the field' from 'derive it', which is the actual question. The right evidence is the replay argument above, and it was not offered.

The implementer's table says both 'carry a positive control in the same test'; they do, but that control asserts the LEDGER ENTRY exists, not that the SIGNAL renders, so it does not defend against a dead selector. Both are killed by other mutations (N9 and N17 -- I re-ran both), so coverage is real; the CLAIM about their positive controls is looser than stated.

triage_candidates.statement: TC-A: the engine accepts any --authority string on amend/waive, so 'human ratification' is a convention nothing enforces. An agent can self-authorize an amendment by typing a string. Candidate: an allowlist, or a distinct marker for self-caught amendments.

TC-B: mutations N15 and N16 are both killed only by test_compliance_line_names_the_count_and_the_latest_begin. Two defect shapes with a single point of coverage; if that test is ever simplified both go uncaught.

TC-C: the g4 log's N17 ('+ ledger_note' appended to the SOFT return) is a NameError crash, not a behaviour change -- ledger_note is scoped inside the hard branch. Its reported blast radius of 23 is crash noise. The behavioural form of the same mutation (compute the note in the soft branch) still kills the named test with a TOTAL of 1. Candidate: a rule that a mutation must not make the module raise, so a crash is never reported as a kill.

TC-D: the Trip section now assembles the same band judgment (fill, hard, model, gate) by hand at three sites and passes it as 7 loose parameters. Candidate for a later Trip-section consolidation once g2/g3/g4 have all settled -- deliberately NOT done inside this diff, which is forbidden from touching what g2/g3 shipped.

TC-E: 'outcome' is a bare string whose two legal values live in three places that must agree by convention (the writer's two call sites and the selector's tuple literal). A named constant would make mutation N10's defect shape structurally impossible rather than test-caught.
